evidence.title: Macworld
evidence.text: Macworld is a web site dedicated to products and software of Apple Inc., published by Mac Publishing, which is headquartered in San Francisco, California.

evidence.title: Macworld
evidence.text: It started life as a print magazine in 1984 and had the largest audited circulation (both total and newsstand) of Macintosh-focused magazines in North America, more than double its nearest competitor, "MacLife" (formerly "MacAddict").

evidence.title: Macworld
evidence.text: "Macworld" was founded by David Bunnell (publisher) and Andrew Fluegelman (editor).

evidence.title: Macworld
evidence.text: It was the oldest Macintosh magazine still in publication, until September 10, 2014, when IDG, its parent company, announced it was discontinuing the print edition and laid off most of the staff, while continuing an online version.

evidence.text: Viscount Powerscourt ( ) is a title that has been created three times in the Peerage of Ireland, each time for members of the Wingfield family.

evidence.title: Viscount Powerscourt
evidence.text: However, this creation became extinct on his death in 1634.

evidence.title: Viscount Powerscourt
evidence.text: However, the 1665 creation also became extinct on the death of its first holder in 1717.

evidence.title: Soaps In Depth
evidence.text: Soaps In Depth is a series of magazines created in 1997 by Bauer Publications to give American soap opera viewers more variety in their soap-related magazine purchases.

evidence.title: Soaps In Depth
evidence.text: Instead of buying a magazine like "Soap Opera Digest", in which all soap operas are covered, "Soaps In Depth" gave the soap viewer and potential shopper individual choices from the "Big Three" networks: ABC Soaps In Depth, CBS Soaps In Depth, and NBC Soaps In Depth.

evidence.title: Soaps In Depth
evidence.text: Each magazine is devoted to only the shows on the network the edition covers and is published biweekly.

evidence.title: Soap Opera Update
evidence.text: Soap Opera Update was a magazine dedicated to the coverage of soap operas, co-founded by Angela Shapiro in 1988.

evidence.title: Soap Opera Update
evidence.text: The magazine was published every three week.

evidence.title: Soap Opera Update
evidence.text: It was purchased by Bauer Media Group in 1992.

evidence.title: Soap Opera Update
evidence.text: The magazine became popular on newsstands in the mid-1990s.

evidence.title: Soap Opera Update
evidence.text: However, due to a lack of subscriptions and promotion, and criticisms for mediocre content and "lazy" press coverage, the magazine was discontinued in late 2002.

evidence.title: Soap Opera Update
evidence.text: In 2006, the "Update" began issuing "Soaps In Depth" and releasing an annual issue to review the soaps of the past year and preview soaps for the new year.
